Abstract:
Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms equipped with reconfigurable intelligent
surfaces (RIS) restore millimetre-wave
connectivity in dense urban environments where severe building blockages sever
direct base-station links. However, coordinating an aerial swarm couples complex
three-dimensional (3D) flight dynamics, user association, directional relaying,
coherent inter-UAV interference, battery depletion, and terrestrial eavesdropper
exposure.

participation from physical propagation and platform constraints.

Research Focus and Core Contributions:
Urban mmWave aerial communication networks face severe challenges from building blockage, inter-UAV inter-
ference, battery drain, and passive eavesdropping.

federated multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework designed specifically for swarms of UAVs carry-
ing reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS). Building directly upon and extending recent advances published in
Vehicular Communications on UAV-assisted multi-RIS networks, aerial energy eﬀiciency, and federated learning,

3. Extensive Benchmarking and Empirical Validation: In extensive 3000-episode simulations with 12 UAVs, 50
ground users, and 72 urban buildings, FedMAPPO achieves 7446 bit/J of fairness-weighted energy eﬀiciency
(+136.4% over decentralized IPPO and +113% to +170% over centralized PPO, SAC, TD3, and EPPO-
inspired baselines, pHolm ≤0.003), reducing unserved ground users from ∼14–20 to 1.75.

1. Introduction
In dense urban environments,
geometric blockage
dominates wireless coverage more severely than trans-
mit power: buildings frequently sever direct line-of-sight
(LoS) links between base stations (BSs) and ground users,
extinguishing millimetre-wave signals.
Unmanned aerial
vehicles (UAVs) establish flexible alternative propagation
paths by leveraging three-dimensional (3D) mobility to
circumvent obstacles [1, 2].
Furthermore, mounting re-

opagation
paths by leveraging three-dimensional (3D) mobility to
circumvent obstacles [1, 2].
Furthermore, mounting re-
configurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) on UAVs enhances
spectral and energy eﬀiciency by passively steering inci-
dent waves without dedicated radio-frequency chains [3, 4].
Aerial RIS deployment transforms the reflection point into
a controllable spatial variable, synthesizing reflected paths
where direct links are blocked [5–7].

In aerial swarms, physical constraints

the same urban blockage that impedes service, stranding
models computed behind buildings.

2. Physics-gated federated multi-agent architecture:
Each UAV autonomously trains an on-board actor-
critic policy to optimize 3D displacement and a
service bid resolved by capacity-constrained match-
ing. An explicit physical eligibility gate admits only
UAVs with viable LoS uplinks and suﬀicient battery
headroom, while the framework supports FedAvg,
FedProx, and resource-aware multi-metric aggrega-
tion.

derive closed-form eavesdropper Dirichlet array gains

rections demonstrate that FedMAPPO achieves

centralized baselines), while slashing unserved users
from 13.9–20.0 to 1.75.
